noteRef.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specPoints.text: understand how enzyme function can be affected by changes in pH altering the active site

primer.text: pH changes enzyme activity just as temperature does, but with a twist: different enzymes prefer different optimum pH values depending on where they work. This note explains why drifting away from the optimum disrupts the active site, why stomach and duodenum enzymes disagree, and why 'denatured' — never 'died' — is the word to write.

lessons.title: Optimum pH values and the denaturation drift
lessons.opening: Most enzymes do their best work at pH 7, but location changes the target: stomach enzymes work in acid near pH 2, and duodenum enzymes prefer alkaline conditions around pH 8 or 9. Drift too far either way and the bonds holding the amino acid chain are disrupted, the active site changes shape, and activity collapses.
keyPoints: Most enzymes have an optimum pH of about 7.
Stomach enzymes work in acidic conditions with an optimum near pH 2.
Duodenum enzymes prefer alkaline conditions, around pH 8 or 9.
Too high or too low a pH disrupts the bonds holding the amino acid chain, changing the active site's shape.

low.restatement: Enzymes peak at their optimum pH — usually 7, sometimes 2 (stomach) or 8-9 (duodenum). Far from it, the site distorts and activity stops.
low.analogy: Each enzyme has a favourite seat on the pH bus; shove it a few seats along and it can still sit, shove it off the bus entirely and it never rides again.
low.examPointer: Pair the location with the number — stomach with pH 2, duodenum with pH 8-9 — because the location marks are attached to the values.

medium.restatement: pH acts through the same shape-destroying pathway as heat: ionisation changes disrupt intramolecular bonds, the complementary site fit is lost, and the rate falls — reversibly near the optimum, terminally far from it.
medium.analogy: pH is a magnet bank beside a paper model: slide it and the folds (bonds) pull open; slide too far and the model creases into a shape that will not hold again.
medium.examPointer: Write 'denatured', not 'killed' or 'died' — the exam hint flags this wording explicitly.

check.stem: What is the optimum pH for most enzymes?

options.explanation: Strongly alkaline conditions denature most enzymes.

check.stem: Why can a stomach enzyme and a duodenum enzyme have different optimum pH values?

options.text: Because pH does not actually affect enzymes
Because each is produced for the conditions of the place where it works
options.explanation: The note ties optima to the acidic or alkaline conditions of production site.

options.text: Because duodenum enzymes are denatured by design

check.stem: What happens to an enzyme's activity as pH moves far from its optimum?

options.text: The enzyme becomes a different substrate
Only the colour of the solution changes
The active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits and activity stops
options.explanation: The shape-loss pathway is the pH mechanism.

options.text: Activity rises because the enzyme is stretched
options.explanation: Stretching distorts, it does not improve.

check.stem: Which wording should you use when writing about an enzyme that has lost its shape at extreme pH?

options.explanation: Enzymes are molecules, not living things.
Rest implies recovery that denaturation does not allow.

check.stem: Which pairing of location and optimum pH is correct?

options.text: Stomach — about pH 2; duodenum — about pH 8 or 9
Stomach — about pH 8; duodenum — about pH 2

check.stem: State the optimum pH of stomach enzymes.
Name the chains whose holding bonds are disrupted by extreme pH.
check.modelAnswer: The amino acid chains that make up the protein.

check.stem: Explain why moving a duodenum enzyme into the acid of the stomach would end its working life even if it were later returned to alkaline conditions.
check.modelAnswer: Far from its alkaline optimum the acidic pH disrupts the bonds holding the enzyme's shape, so its active site no longer complements its substrate; because that denaturation is irreversible, returning it to alkaline conditions cannot rebuild the working shape.

check.stem: An indigestion tablet neutralises excess stomach acid. Using this note, state what happens to stomach-enzyme activity and to a swallowed duodenum-type enzyme as the pH rises.
check.modelAnswer: The stomach enzyme drifts above its acidic optimum and loses activity as its site distorts, while a duodenum-type enzyme moves closer to ITS alkaline optimum and works better — same pH change, opposite outcomes, because optima are location-specific.

glossary.definition: The pH at which an enzyme's activity is greatest.
Describes conditions above pH 7, such as those in the duodenum.
Describes conditions below pH 7, such as those in the stomach.
